Step 4 — HEX data

⚠ This step depends on the hex data access pipeline, which is under active development. The design is specified in arch-11. Functions described below do not yet exist in the package — this page documents the intended workflow.

What HEX data is

Pre-computed indicator values stored at H3 hexagonal resolution 6 (~36 km² per cell) in online parquet files maintained by the project team. Each parquet contains one or more indicator columns keyed by H3 hex index, with an optional time dimension (one row per hex × year).

The hex data pipeline lets you:

  1. Browse available indicators via a package-shipped registry.
  2. Fetch values for only the hexagons covering your country’s boundaries.
  3. Aggregate hex values to your admin polygons using configurable weighting and aggregation strategies.
  4. Produce a standard metadata-hex.xlsx that Step 5’s compile_pti_data() merges with your user metadata.

Population is always fetched automatically from the registry and is used for population-weighted aggregation. It also appears as a visible indicator in the deployed app.

Prerequisites

Step 1 must be complete. You need:

  • app-data/shapes.rds containing your admin layers and an admin9_Hexagon layer built by make_hex_grid() and enriched by make_admin_lookup().
my_shp    <- readRDS("app-data/shapes.rds")
hex_layer <- my_shp$admin9_Hexagon
hex_ids   <- hex_layer$admin9Pcod

Discovering available variables 

list_hex_vars()

Returns a tibble — one row per registered variable — showing canonical name, display name, units, pillar, whether it has a time dimension, available years (hint from registry), and default aggregation strategy.

Filter by pillar or temporal status:

list_hex_vars(pillar = "Economic Activity")
list_hex_vars(temporal = TRUE)

To query the live parquet for actual available years (not just the registry hint):

get_available_years(vars = NULL, "nightlights")
#> nightlights (PTI Pre-computed Hex Data): 2013 2014 2015 ... 2022

Selecting variables and years 

vars <- use_hex_vars(
  "nightlights",
  "poverty_rate",
  "population",
  years = c(2015, 2022)
)

years applies globally to all temporal variables. Non-temporal variables (like a static poverty estimate) are returned regardless.

Year resolution rules:

  • Exact year available → used as-is.
  • Exact year absent → nearest available year substituted. On equidistant tie, the later year is preferred. A warning is emitted.
  • No data within 7 years of a requested year → error with available years listed.

In an interactive session with years = NULL, the system prints available years and prompts you to choose. In a non-interactive session (e.g. quarto render), years = NULL errors with an actionable message.

Fetching hex data 

hex_data <- fetch_hex_data(hex_ids = hex_ids, vars = vars)

Only hexagons matching your hex_ids are read (parquet predicate pushdown). Temporal variables are pivoted wide: nightlights_2015, nightlights_2022. Population is always the first indicator column after hex_id.

Resolution bridge: if your hex grid is at H5 (coarser than the H6 source data), fetch_hex_data() transparently expands each H5 cell to its H6 children, fetches at H6, and aggregates back to H5. Requesting finer than H6 (e.g. H7) produces an error.

Progress is reported per variable.

Optional: merging your own data

If you have project-specific indicators in a local parquet file, merge them between fetch and aggregate:

my_data <- arrow::open_dataset("data-raw/conflict.parquet") |>
  dplyr::filter(h3id %in% hex_ids) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::rename(hex_id = h3id) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = year,
    values_from = conflict_events,
    names_prefix = "conflict_"
  )

hex_data <- dplyr::full_join(hex_data, my_data, by = "hex_id")

Local parquet contract:

Requirement Rule
Format Readable by arrow::open_dataset()
Layout Long format — one row per hex × time period
Hex column Any name — you rename to hex_id before merge
Population Absent (comes from registry)
Values Numeric columns, one per indicator
Uniqueness No duplicate hex ID per time period

Aggregating to admin polygons 

aggregated <- aggregate_hex_to_shapes(
  hex_data  = hex_data,
  hex_layer = hex_layer,
  shp_dta   = my_shp,
  strategy  = list(
    .default    = c(weight = "pop",  fun = "mean"),
    nightlights = c(weight = "none", fun = "mean"),
    population  = c(weight = "none", fun = "sum"),
    conflict    = c(weight = "none", fun = "sum")
  )
)

Strategy has two orthogonal dimensions:

  • weight: "pop" (population-weighted), "area" (area-weighted), or "none" (unweighted / plutocratic).
  • fun: "mean", "median", "sum", "min", "max".

A .default entry covers all variables not explicitly listed. For temporal variables, use the stem name (e.g. nightlights covers both nightlights_2015 and nightlights_2022).

Aggregation is always hex → each admin level directly (hex→admin1, hex→admin2, etc.) — never chained through intermediate levels.

NA values are treated as 0. If all hexes in a polygon are NA for a variable, the result is NA with a warning.

Building the metadata Excel 

build_hex_metadata(
  aggregated       = aggregated,
  shp_dta          = my_shp,
  indicator_config = tibble::tibble(
    canonical_name        = "conflict",
    var_name              = "Conflict Events ({year})",
    var_description       = "ACLED conflict event count.",
    var_units             = "count",
    pillar_group          = 4,
    pillar_name           = "Security",
    legend_revert_colours = TRUE,
    fltr_exclude_pti      = FALSE
  ),
  country_name = "Rwanda",
  output_path  = "app-data/metadata-hex.xlsx",
  include_hex  = INCLUDE_HEX_IN_APP
)

Registry variables have their metadata auto-populated from the YAML — you only need indicator_config for non-registry variables (your local parquet indicators). You can override any registry default via indicator_config.

Temporal variables expand to one metadata row per resolved year, with var_name generated from the glue template (e.g. "Night Lights (2015)").

The INCLUDE_HEX_IN_APP switch

Set in 00-master.R:

INCLUDE_HEX_IN_APP <- FALSE
Value Behaviour
TRUE Hex-level admin9_Hexagon sheet included in metadata Excel. Hex polygons shipped with the app.
FALSE (default) Hex sheet omitted. Only aggregated admin-level sheets written. All hex-sourced indicator values still available at admin levels.

When include_hex is not set and the hex grid exceeds 5,000 cells, the system warns and prompts interactively (defaults to FALSE in non-interactive sessions).

Supported admin levels

Hex-derived indicators appear on every admin-level sheet in the output Excel (admin1, admin2, etc.). spatial_level in the metadata sheet points to the hex level (e.g. admin9_Hexagon) — the finest available level.

Note on ordering

This step is order-flexible — it can run before or after Step 3. The two outputs (metadata-user.xlsx and metadata-hex.xlsx) are independent intermediate files merged by Step 5’s compile_pti_data().
